summary: @servicetitan/anvil-icons preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled payload unrelated to the icons library
details: The package declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"` in package.json. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip`, extracts and chmods the binary, then invokes it via execFileSync against `math_init.js`, a 727 KB `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle shipped in the tarball. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated: setup.mjs uses obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` renaming with wrapper-call indirection, and math_init.js is a Bun-compiled bundle with a rotated string-array (`function WV8StW(...) {... MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())... } const n7gIxM=[0x0,0x1,...]`) and hex-named symbols. The advertised purpose per README is generating a React `<Icon>` component from Material Design SVGs; the shipped `dist/index.js` main is an ordinary React SVG bundle. There is no legitimate reason for an icons library to fetch a second language runtime and hand it an opaque compiled payload before the package is required. Installing this version causes an obfuscated payload to execute on the installer's machine under a Node-invisible runtime at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
